title: Relative global complete intersections are flat
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n,c\ge0$, and $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$. Suppose $S=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. Then $R\to S$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak q\subset S$ and let $\mathfrak q'$ be its inverse image in $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$. Part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-partial-local-flat], with $i=c$, says that $P_{\mathfrak q'}/(f_1,\dots,f_c)P_{\mathfrak q'}$ is flat over $R$. The prime-localization isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient], applied to the ideal $(f_1,\dots,f_c)\subset P$, identifies this ring with $S_{\mathfrak q}$ over $R$. Thus $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat as an $R$-module.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SW (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection), invoking Lemma Tag 00SV (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-conormal), part (2); localization of a quotient is Proposition Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient)

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be the inverse image of $\mathfrak q$. Since $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is an $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module and is flat over $R$ by the preceding step, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization] (the direction from flatness over $R$ to flatness over $R_{\mathfrak p}$) makes $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ flat. This holds for every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $S$, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-map-local-criterion] gives flatness of $R\to S$. If $S=0$, there are no prime ideals, and the same local criterion applies vacuously.
